item.title: Winter Painting Leads Thomaston Place Auction
item.description: THOMASTON, MAINE — Fitting with the blizzard that hit the East Coast on Sunday, February 22, an Andrew George Winter (American, 1893-1958) painting was the top lot of Thomaston Place Auction Galleries’ Winter Enchantment auction that ran February 20-22. item.title: Birger Sandzén Commands $76,700 In Soulis’ Art Auction
item.description: LONE JACK, MO. — A 1923 Birger Sandzén painting titled “Pines by the Lake, Estes Park” soared past its $35/$50,000 estimate to attain $76,700, including buyer’s premium, at Soulis Auctions’ 20th annual Winter Art Auction on February 22. item.title: Across The Block
item.description: Auctions nationwide were an art collector’s dream this past week, as John Lennon’s 1970 “Bag One” portfolio, full of 14 lithographs, sold at Clars for $41,600. Fine art also did well, as an oil on board depicting Chillon Castle near Montreaux, Switzerland, by Hermann O. Herzog was raised to $7,980 at Schwenke. item.title: Silver & Fine Art Are First Choice At Sloans & Kenyon
item.description: CHEVY CHASE, MD. — Various antiques, painting and sculpture, ancient pottery, black-and-white photographs, silver, decorative arts, rugs, Asian ceramics and works of art, jewelry, coins and clocks were among the offerings in Sloans & Kenyon’s February Estate Catalogue Auction, conducted on the 12th of the month. item.title: Custer’s Proclamation Earns Bold Price At Heritage
item.description: DALLAS — Heritage Auctions’ February 26 sale of Historical Manuscripts & Texana featured 457 lots and realized $2.5 million in total sales from more than 5,000 registered bidders. Significant lots included items related to the Gettysburg Address and additional Lincoln material; autographs from other presidents, military leaders and artists; the first book printed in the Republic of Texas; and a signed letter from Marie Antoinette. item.title: Funerary Stele Marks Top Price At Sworders
item.description: ESSEX, UK — Leading Sworders Fine Art Auctioneers’ February 24 auction featuring the collection of veteran antiques dealer Peter Petrou was a Greek marble funerary stele from the Hellenistic period, Second-First Century BCE, that attained $33,000, including the buyer’s premium. The stele was in the form of a naiskos, enclosing a rectangular recessed panel carved in high relief. A complete report will appear in an upcoming edition. item.title: Paris Expo Ewer Catches Attention At Tremont
item.description: SUDBURY, MASS. — An 1867 Paris Exposition champlevé-enameled Etruscan Revival silver ewer on stand by Gustave Baugrand became the top lot in Tremont Auctions’ March 1 sale of fine arts, antiques and jewelry. item.title: Pig Painting Farms Big Win For Everard
item.description: SAVANNAH, GA. — Three days of auction action at Everard Auctions & Appraisals led to 1,339 lots crossing the block between February 24-26. An acrylic on canvas painting by John Wesley (New York/California, b 1928) was the highest-earning lot of all three days, selling on day one, which featured fine and decorative art from the estate of interior designer Arthur B. item.title: Cheryl Ann McGrath, Antiques Dealer, 67
item.description: SCITUATE, MASS. — Cheryl Ann (Giannino) McGrath, 67, of Scituate returned to her lord on December 31, 2025. She was the beloved wife of James “Butch” McGrath, Jr, with whom she shared 33 years of marriage and 41 years of life.
